visuals.title: Where it happens
visuals.text: Infection of breast tissue, usually while breastfeeding; S. aureus is the usual organism.

visuals.title: Which test?
nodes: No lump: clinical diagnosis of mastitis

events.x: Keep breastfeeding and expressing; paracetamol or ibuprofen
No better, cracked nipple, or unwell: start antibiotics

glossary.Milk expression: Emptying milk from the breast by hand or pump rather than by the baby feeding.
glossary.Childbearing age: The years a woman can become pregnant, roughly from puberty to menopause.
glossary.Paracetamol: A simple painkiller that also lowers fever.
glossary.Ibuprofen: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used for pain, inflammation and fever.
glossary.Penicillin allergic: Having an allergic reaction to penicillin-type antibiotics, so flucloxacillin must be avoided.
glossary.Breast ultrasound: Imaging with sound waves that shows fluid collections such as abscesses in the breast.
glossary.Gold standard: The best available test or treatment against which others are judged.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination alone, without tests.
glossary.Nipple discharge: Fluid leaking from the nipple, such as pus or blood-stained fluid.
glossary.Flu-like symptoms: Fever, aches, chills and tiredness similar to influenza.
glossary.Colonisation: Bacteria living and multiplying on or in tissue, which may lead to infection.
glossary.Coalesce: To merge together into one mass.
glossary.Walled-off: Surrounded by a fibrous capsule, separating the pus from surrounding tissue.
glossary.Pus: Thick fluid made of dead white cells, bacteria and tissue debris.
glossary.Oral flora: The normal bacteria that live in the mouth.
glossary.Systemically unwell: Ill throughout the body, e.g. fever, tachycardia, feeling very unwell, not just local symptoms.
glossary.Duct: A small tube in the breast that carries milk to the nipple.
glossary.Referral: Sending the patient to another specialist team for assessment or treatment.
glossary.Culture: Growing bacteria from a sample in the lab to identify them and their antibiotic sensitivities.
glossary.Antibiotics: Drugs that kill bacteria or stop them growing.
